newsitem.title: FRANCE: SNCF to decide on telecoms partner on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: SNCF to decide on telecoms partner on Wednesday.

text.p: France's state-run railroads group SNCF will on Wednesday take a decision about an industrial partner to run its telecommunications network as a so-called alternative infrastructure in 1998.

A spokesman for the rail company said the decision would be taken during a board meeting on Wednesday and he denied market rumours the SNCF had decided to select Bouygues Telecom and its Italian partner STET.
"Nothing has been decided. There is a board meeting on February 12 where the matter will be discussed," an SNCF spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
French Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon in December granted a 15-year telecoms operating licence to SNCF's Telecom Developpement unit.

The SNCF licence covers the railroads' existing network of 8,000 kilometres of optic fibre all over the country, as well as radio links, which will be expanded to some 12,000 kilometres in the next six years, SNCF sources said.
SNCF is seeking an industrial partner to buy a stake in Telecom Developpement and run the network. It has three offers from interested companies.

One is from Cegetel, the Generale des Eaux unit in which British Telecom Plc and Mannesmann of Germany have a stake and which aims to become France's second biggest operator. It already runs the SFR mobile network.
Another is from Bouygues and STET.
A third offer is from the Unisource consortium made up of Dutch KPN, Telia AB of Sweden, Swiss Telecom PTT and Spain's Telefonica which may or may not involve AT&T of the United States.
The SNCF network could be a vital part in any operator's plans, cutting the time to set up a network in time for the 1998 start of competition as well as reducing investment needs.

Telecom Developpement, like any future rival to France Telecom, will have to contribute to the costs of running the public service of telecommunications which will remain assured by the national operator.
A first tranche of 20 percent in France Telecom is expected to be floated on this spring.
